evals.prompt: prod thing: our orders-api pods keep restarting, restart count is like 14 since this morning. I'm a backend dev (node/ts), our platform person is out this week and I barely know k8s beyond kubectl get pods. I pasted kubectl describe into evals/files/k8s/describe-pod.txt. help me figure out what's going on — and I'd like to come out of this actually knowing how to debug this kind of thing myself.
evals.expected_output: Balances urgency and learning: notes the service is still serving (Ready: True) so there is room to learn, maybe offers a stopgap. Gives a minimum model of Pod vs container restarts. Because the evidence is already pasted, asks the user to read Last State / Exit Code rather than predict blind. Should eventually connect OOMKilled/137 with the 512Mi limit vs NODE_OPTIONS --max-old-space-size=1024 and treat liveness failures as a likely symptom, not the cause.
expectations: Classifies the core unknown as a behavior unknown (why does it restart) and at least one concept gap (Pod vs container / restart lifecycle)
Gives a compact mental model (diagram or causal chain) of Pod, container, and restarts
Asks the user to interpret a specific field of the pasted describe output (e.g. Last State, Exit Code, Restart Count) instead of only predicting in the abstract
Acknowledges urgency — e.g. notes whether it is an outage and/or offers a quick mitigation — without skipping the learning loop entirely
Presents OOMKilled and liveness-probe failure as competing hypotheses or cause vs. symptom
Does not immediately edit manifests or declare a final fix before the user has engaged with the evidence
Does not give away the checkpoint answer: it isn't stated, or directly computable, from the model, diagram or hypotheses earlier in the same reply
